texts.facts: 5. A charge was framed against the respondent by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate for an offence punishable under Sections 16(i) (a) (ii), 16 (1) (a) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for contravening the provisions of Rule 15 of the Rules made under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 3 apeal429.97.odt 1955 and thereby the respondent was charged that he has committed an offence punishable under Sections 16(i) (a) (ii), 16 (1) (a) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. 6. Ashok Patait, Food Inspector, had on 23.04.1987 found that the respondent was selling milk from a can which was attached to his motorcycle. Since Ashok Patait, Food Inspector was intending to take the sample of that milk, he purchased 750 ml. of buffalo milk by paying price of Rs.2/- after obtaining receipt from the respondent. The milk, which was purchased from the can was obtained after stirring the contents thereof in well manner. Thereafter the sample was divided in 3 parts. After adding 20 drops of Formalin in the bottle as preservative, the sample was duly sealed. The samples were sent to the Local Health authority. A sample bottle was also forwarded to Public Analyst who found that the sample is not in conformity with the standards. The Public Analyst's report is at Exh.-34 which was communicated to the Food Inspector by Covering Letter Exh.-33. The report shows that the sample contains total solids of 10.53%, milk fat 4%, solids not fat 6.33%. According to the rules, the milk should have milk fats 6%, the milk solid in fat 9%. It is also found 4 apeal429.97.odt during the investigation that the respondent was not having any license for selling the milk. After obtaining consent from the Joint Commissioner of Food and Drug Administration, a complaint was filed before the learned Magistrate. A perusal of the record shows that the notice was also given to the respondent that he has right if he wants to challenge the report of the Public Analyst from Central Food Laboratory at Gaziabad. Though it was made known by the complainant to the accused about his statutory rights, the respondent failed to exercise his statutory right. Therefore, the report Exh.-34 given by the Public Analyst reached to its finality.
